paper.title: NavGPT: Explicit Reasoning in Vision-and-Language Navigation with Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: NavGPT is a purely LLM-based, zero-shot vision-and-language navigation agent that reads textual descriptions of observations, history and explorable directions and reasons explicitly; it exhibits high-level planning but falls short of trained models on R2R.
paper.scope_decision: in_scope (A): frozen GPT-4/3.5 harness with VFM translators, history summariser and a prompt manager controlling a navigating agent over the Matterport3D R2R graph, closed loop in simulation.

preliminary_judgment: Written after reading the fixed text, before opening this paper's seat records: system_method (with an analysis framing); R2R val-unseen, 783 trajectories, standard 3 m SR, single run; SR 34 vs trained 52-72; no same-LLM alternative harness; ablations with GPT-3.5 on a 216-sample split drawn from training and val-unseen scenes, used to pick the FoV; depth from the simulator; no repeats, no cost. Expected online, scoped; measurement capped by the single-run clause; causality weak.

signatures.object: text-only LLM navigation agent (GPT-4 / GPT-3.5) in Matterport3D R2R with a prompt manager, navigation-system-principle prompt, history buffer
signatures.information: instruction; per-direction text descriptions of 24 egocentric views (BLIP-2 captions of 3 elevations, GPT-3.5-summarised), Faster-RCNN objects within 3 m with relative heading and simulator depth, navigable viewpoint IDs with angle/distance from the simulator graph; summarised past observations plus own thoughts and actions
signatures.operation: per step output Thought then Action (viewpoint ID or stop), ReAct-style
signatures.output: next viewpoint on the navigation graph; episode ends on stop
signatures.conditions: discrete navigation graph, ground-truth depth of detected objects, nothing trained for VLN
signatures.feedback: new observation after moving; no separate verifier
signatures.selection_rule_or_data: none; LLM decides stop; ablations use GPT-3.5
signatures.persistence: history buffer with GPT-3.5 summariser inside the episode
signatures.later_use: history re-read at each step; nothing across episodes
signatures.claimed_effect: zero-shot R2R val-unseen SR 34 / SPL 29 / OSR 42 / NE 6.46 (GPT-4); explicit planning visible in thoughts
signatures.failure_boundary: caption information loss, summarisation loss, object tracking, premature stop

signatures.object: visual-observation granularity and auxiliary channels (FoV/views, objects, depth)
signatures.operation: choose FoV 45 deg / 24 views; add object list; add depth
signatures.output: language descriptions fed to the LLM
signatures.conditions: BLIP-2 caption quality depends on FoV
signatures.selection_rule_or_data: chosen on a 216-sample split built from train and val-unseen scenes (GPT-3.5)
signatures.claimed_effect: SR +6.5 over 60-deg variant, +4.9 for objects, +0.7 for depth

gap.author_gap: The reasoning ability of LLMs for embodied navigation is under-explored; trained VLN agents' decisions are implicit and generalize poorly.
gap.checked_gap: Reasoning traces are shown for selected examples, and a real performance gap to trained models is measured (SR 34 vs 66). The paper does not test whether the explicit reasoning is what produces the 34, and the LGX neighbour is not run.
lineage: ReAct + visual-captioning pipelines + LLM-as-parser/commonsense for navigation (Shah et al., Zhou et al., LGX) -> NavGPT (end-to-end LLM VLN agent with history and VFM translators)
supervised VLN (Seq2Seq ... HAMT, DuET) = the trained class used for comparison

closest_adjacent.name: LGX
closest_adjacent.solved: LLM commonsense for object navigation with GLIP-based stop

gap.residue: Information lost in turning pixels into text and in summarising history is identified as the bottleneck; the paper does not test remedies beyond FoV, objects and depth.
gap.stakes: Zero-shot, inspectable instruction-following navigation without VLN training data.
gap.method_response: Translate vision to text with VFMs, give the LLM a ReAct loop with history and a navigation principle prompt, and read the thoughts.
gap.remaining_gap: Large gap to trained models; hand-off of visual details; stopping; sim only (authors); no ablation of the reasoning trace or history summariser (ours).
gap.unresolved: Neighbour papers not pinned in the batch materials; empty comparisons do not show novelty.
gap.aggregate_note: son55 gap retained: whether the explicit reasoning produces the 34% SR is not tested, and LGX is not run.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop simulator navigation with geometry-judged success; one dataset/simulator, with design explored on overlapping scenes, so not transfer.
assessment.author_claim_preserved: NavGPT is a purely LLM-based, zero-shot vision-and-language navigation agent that reads textual descriptions of observations, history and explorable directions and reasons explicitly; it exhibits high-level planning but falls short of trained models on R2R.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A zero-shot GPT-4 agent that sees only BLIP-2/detector text descriptions and a navigable-viewpoint list reaches SR 34 / SPL 29 on R2R val-unseen (783 trajectories in the 11 unseen environments; whether 783 or 3x783 instruction episodes is not stated) in one run, well below trained models (SR up to 72). The qualitative thoughts look plan-like, but their contribution to success is untested.

G.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. A concrete gap (whether an LLM can reason and act explicitly for instruction-following VLN; trained agents' decisions are implicit) with named neighbours (LGX, CLIP-based zero-shot VLN) and an honest residual (caption information loss, history summarisation). Neighbours are not compared.

M.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Text serialisation (BLIP-2 captions, detector objects with simulator depth, navigable candidates) plus a ReAct loop with summarised history is reconstructible, and the FoV/object ablations are consistent with the diagnosis. The central "explicit reasoning" prediction is never contrasted with a no-thought or caption-only variant.

X.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Stages, models, FoV/view counts, object radius, depth source and summariser are specified. The system prompt and history formats appear only in figures, GPT version and decoding settings are not given, and stopping is decided by the LLM alone.

measurement.reason: Resolved toward sol (son55 3). The standard R2R metrics (SR within 3 m, OSR, SPL, NE, TL) are geometry-checked by the simulator on the full val-unseen set. But every reported number is a single run, and anchor v2 states "all results single runs without repetition -> rating <=2". The denominator is also ambiguous: the text says 783 trajectories, while R2R pairs each trajectory with three instructions (SEC-1).

causality.reason: Both seats 1; confirmed. The headline claim about explicit reasoning has no control. The component studies are a cumulative FoV/object/depth stack on 216 GPT-3.5 samples whose increments (+0.7 SR for depth, about 1.5 episodes) sit within noise. The only non-training baseline is an untrained supervised model, and GPT-4 (headline) and GPT-3.5 (ablations) are never crossed.

holdout.reason: Both seats 2; confirmed. Zero-shot on R2R val-unseen is held out for the LLM, but the design split mixes training and val-unseen scenes (agg:E002) and was used to choose the interface (rule 2). Development overlap and GPT-4 contamination are not addressed, and only one benchmark is used.

statistics.reason: Both seats 1; confirmed. Single run for every number, no variance/CI, no repeated GPT-4 runs, no counted failure breakdown (qualitative only). Anchor v2: no repeats, no failure decomposition -> <=1.
